 US News Agregar Clarín en X Social Security benefit dates 2026: Who gets paid on October 21, full schedule, and upcoming calendar shifts
 Mark your calendars: A federal holiday and weekend dates are shifting Social Security and SSI payment days for November and December 2026. Here is the full breakdown of when your checks will land in your account.
 Navigating your monthly benefits for the remainder of 2026? The Social Security Administration (SSA) is rolling out key calendar adjustments for November and December. NEWSROOM CLARIN For the nearly 72 million Americans relying on monthly disbursements from the Social Security Administration (SSA) —including retired workers, disabled individuals, and surviving dependents— tracking the calendar over the final quarter of 2026 involves several critical schedule adjustments .
 While traditional monthly payments follow a predictable rotation dictated by birth dates, upcoming federal holidays and calendar quirks will shift deposit dates for millions of recipients in November and December . Most notably, a federal holiday next month will trigger an early payment for early-month birthdays, while Supplemental Security Income (SSI) recipients must budget around back-to-back checks that leave November with no payment at all.
 Standard Distribution: How the SSA Staggers Payments
 For beneficiaries who filed for Social Security benefits after May 1997 , monthly checks are distributed on Wednesdays based on the recipient's day of birth:
 Birthdays from the 1st through the 10th: Paid on the second Wednesday of the month.
 Birthdays from the 11th through the 20th: Paid on the third Wednesday of the month.
 Birthdays from the 21st through the 31st: Paid on the fourth Wednesday of the month.
 The "3rd of the Month" Exception Group:
 A separate schedule applies to beneficiaries who began claiming Social Security prior to May 1997, those who receive both Social Security and SSI benefits, individuals residing abroad, or those whose state covers their Medicare premiums. These individuals receive their Social Security benefits on the 3rd of each month , or on the preceding business day if the 3rd falls on a weekend or federal holiday.
 November and December Calendar Shifts Explained
 The final months of 2026 include notable schedule modifications that beneficiaries should factor into their household budgets:
 The Veterans Day Early Check: In November 2026, Veterans Day falls on Wednesday, November 11—the exact date scheduled for the second Wednesday distribution. Because federal banks and postal operations close for the holiday, beneficiaries born between the 1st and the 10th will receive their funds one business day early, on Tuesday, November 10, 2026.
 The "Double SSI" Dynamic 
 Under federal guidelines, Supplemental Security Income (which supports more than 7 million low-income seniors and individuals with disabilities) is issued on the 1st of each month. When the 1st falls on a weekend or federal holiday, the payment is moved to the closest preceding business day:
 Because November 1 falls on a Sunday, November's SSI payment will be deposited early on Friday, October 30 . Consequently, SSI recipients will receive two checks in October and no payment during the calendar month of November.
 Because New Year's Day (January 1, 2027) is a federal holiday, January’s SSI payment will be issued early on Thursday, December 31, 2026 , resulting in two SSI checks landing in December (Dec. 1 and Dec. 31).
 Complete Payment Calendar for the Remainder of 2026
 October 2026
 Wednesday, Oct. 21: Social Security for birthdays 11th–20th
 Wednesday, Oct. 28: Social Security for birthdays 21st–31st
 Friday, Oct. 30: November SSI payment (issued early due to Nov. 1 falling on a Sunday)
 November 2026
 Tuesday, Nov. 3: Social Security for pre-May 1997 claimants and dual Social Security/SSI recipients
 Tuesday, Nov. 10: Social Security for birthdays 1st–10th (Issued one day early due to Veterans Day on Nov. 11)
 Wednesday, Nov. 18: Social Security for birthdays 11th–20th
 Wednesday, Nov. 25: Social Security for birthdays 21st–31st
 (Note: No SSI payment is issued in November, as it was paid on Oct. 30) 
 December 2026
 Tuesday, Dec. 1: Regular December SSI payment
 Thursday, Dec. 3: Social Security for pre-May 1997 claimants and dual Social Security/SSI recipients
 Wednesday, Dec. 9: Social Security for birthdays 1st–10th
 Wednesday, Dec. 16: Social Security for birthdays 11th–20th
 Wednesday, Dec. 23: Social Security for birthdays 21st–31st
 Thursday, Dec. 31: January 2027 SSI payment (Issued early due to New Year's Day on Jan. 1)
 What About the 2027 COLA Bump?
 On October 14, the SSA officially confirmed a 3.6% Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA) for 2027 , outpacing the 2.8% adjustment implemented in 2026.
 The increase is projected to raise the average retired worker's monthly benefit by approximately $75, lifting average checks from $2,095 to $2,170. For couples receiving dual retirement benefits, combined payments will increase to approximately $3,355, while disabled worker benefits will rise to an average of $1,701. The maximum federal SSI benefit will adjust to $1,029 for individuals and $1,544 for eligible couples.
 Beneficiaries should keep in mind that none of the remaining 2026 payments will reflect the 3.6% boost. The higher payout amounts will begin appearing on regular Social Security checks in January 2027. SSI recipients will be the first to see the adjustment in their bank accounts on December 31, 2026, when their early January benefit is processed. Personalized COLA notices detailing new exact benefit amounts and Medicare Part B premium deductions will become available via online my Social Security accounts starting in late November.
